See Google Calendar and any calendar feed next to HEY, in one grid and one bar.

![OmaCal's calendar and quick-add form](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crmne/omacal/v1.2.0/preview.png)

## New

- **Google Calendar, read and written directly.** Turn on **Google Calendar** under **Calendars from** in OmaCal's settings. It shows every calendar switched on in Google Calendar. New events can go on any Google calendar you can write to. You can edit them for one day or the whole series, including removing reminders, and delete one-off events. No invitations are sent. Signing in is done by gws, Google's Workspace CLI (`sudo pacman -S googleworkspace-cli`, then `gws auth setup` and `gws auth login -s calendar`), so OmaCal stores no Google credentials. Event text goes to Google over HTTPS, never on a command line. By @crmne, building on @dpaluy's approach in [#2](https://github.com/crmne/omacal/pull/2).
- **Calendar feeds.** Paste a `webcal://` or `https://` address into **Calendar feeds** in the settings: a Google calendar's secret address, iCloud or Outlook, a holiday calendar. OmaCal works out repeating events itself, including skipped and moved days and each event's time zone. Feed addresses work like passwords, so they are kept in `~/.config/omacal/feeds.json`, readable only by you. By @crmne.
- **Every service in one place.** HEY, Google and feeds share the grid, the day view, the bar and reminders. If one service fails, the others keep showing. The settings and the event form list each service's calendars under its name, and every change goes to the service the event belongs to. By @crmne.
- **HEY is optional.** Turn off what you do not use. With HEY off, or hey-cli not installed, OmaCal works with Google and feeds alone. By @crmne.

![The event form with HEY and Google calendars](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crmne/omacal/v1.2.0/screenshots/quick-add.png)

## Fixed

- **Hiding a calendar hides only that one.** Turning off a calendar in the settings no longer also hides a calendar with the same name on another service. Names typed into `hiddenCalendars` by hand still hide that name everywhere. By @crmne.
- **Calendars HEY subscribes to are not offered for new events.** HEY cannot write to them (a Google or Todoist calendar added to HEY, for example), so adding an event there used to fail. By @crmne.
- **Error messages show the real exit status.** Messages that included a command's exit status used to say "undefined". By @crmne.

## Known limitations

- **Some Google changes are still Google Calendar's.** For events with guests, OmaCal changes only the reminder, because Google Calendar is where you choose whether guests are emailed. Deleting a repeating event is also left to Google Calendar.
- **Google is checked every few minutes, not live.** Google only pushes changes to a public web address.
- **Signing in to Google needs your own OAuth client.** `gws auth setup` creates one in a Google Cloud project of yours.
- **Feeds are read only**, and are fetched at most every two minutes.
- **A HEY calendar that copies Google shows its events twice** once Google is on. Turn off that HEY calendar in the settings.

## Install

```sh
omarchy plugin add https://github.com/crmne/omacal.git --enable
omarchy plugin disable omarchy.clock
```

Already installed: `omarchy plugin update crmne.omacal`.

## Thanks

@crmne implemented the changes. Thanks to @dpaluy for the first Google Calendar implementation through gws in [#2](https://github.com/crmne/omacal/pull/2), which set the direction for this release.

OmaCal is an independent project, not created by, affiliated with, or supported by HEY, 37signals or Google.
